page: Amazon Web Services m8gn.48xlarge is a general-purpose, network-optimized instance powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. Built on the arm64 architecture, it features 192 dedicated physical cores utilizing the AWS Neoverse-V2 ARMv9 model running at 2.7 GHz. The instance is equipped with 768.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression scores placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, registering top-tier results for both cached small-block reads and uncached large-block read and write operations. The instance also demonstrates top-tier capabilities in database operations, software compilation, and static web serving throughput. Single-core performance, however, falls within the average range across several benchmarks, including stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core tests.

With a baseline network bandwidth of 300 Gbps and optimization for EBS, the instance is designed for high-throughput networking and data transfer tasks. The combination of high multi-core density, substantial memory bandwidth, and high network throughput makes this instance suitable for large-scale database operations, multi-threaded software compilation, high-volume static web serving, and containerized microservices.
